Summary

At a glance

Tier 1 is a single ability an agent can be granted, such as fetching a web page or reading a mailbox. Tier 2 is a family workflow built from those, such as a morning text of what in your mail needs attention. Tier 3 is acting on a device or on the world beyond chat: a computer, a phone, a browser, voice, the house.

The table counts the planned features. The wave chip on each card links to the plan it is built in. Examples on the cards are made up to show the feature; none is a fact about your family. Value and effort are my estimates.

Can Happy control a computer?

On paper yes; not safely on this Mac's own desktop. OpenClaw has a built-in computer tool that takes screenshots and sends clicks and keystrokes. On macOS it works only through the separate OpenClaw Mac app, which is not installed here.

Once that app is paired and has its macOS permissions, the grant has no per-action confirmation, no expiry and no limit to one app, and it works only on an unlocked desktop. On the Mac mini the only unlocked desktop is Happy's own, with Messages signed in, and pairing the app also brings shell execution and desktop sharing with it.

What is planned: a list of commands no paired device may ever run, built first in wave I (MAC-04), and, as the last wave, a pilot on a clean, throwaway virtual Mac with one chore you name (MAC-02, wave J). Its first step tests whether it can work at all, and Happy's own desktop is never used. OpenAI and Anthropic both tell developers to run this kind of tool in an isolated machine. Printing needs no screen control (F080, wave H).

SeeMAC-04 · MAC-02 · F080 · MAC-12 · MAC-07

Can Happy control a connected idle iPhone?

No. The OpenClaw iPhone app makes a phone a sensor and a chat client. It has no command to tap or read other apps, its camera works only while the app is open on screen, and its own documentation says it is not a computer-control backend.

The only way to tap inside iPhone apps is Apple's iPhone Mirroring driven by the Mac computer tool. Apple requires the phone to be signed in to the same Apple Account as the Mac user (Happy's), locked and nearby, and the route inherits every problem in the box above. It was turned down (IPH-08), with developer automation over a cable (IPH-12) and Apple's accessibility features (IPH-13). Every spare-phone idea was removed in review.

What is planned: the OpenClaw app on your own iPhone, for chat with files and, if it passes its check, voice (OCL-01, wave I). A phone running the app is a control console for the whole gateway, not a per-person window, so it is your phone only and Jordan stays on iMessage.

SeeOCL-01 · MAC-04 · IPH-08 · IPH-12 · IPH-13 · IPH-02 · IPH-14

Channel, media and voice 2

F002

Photos and PDFs sent to Happy are read and answered

Needs a buildMedium riskAdultsValue 5/5Effort SWave B

Send a photo of a flyer, label or receipt, or a PDF packet, and Happy reads it and answers questions about it; today a message that is only an attachment is dropped without a reply. Nothing on the Mac screens what a parent sends: the photo or PDF goes to the cloud model as it is, which Tony accepted on 12 Oct. The house rule goes on the printed sheet: no bank, tax or medical papers.

Example: A parent sends a photo of a school flyer from the third-grader's class and asks 'what do we need to send in, and by when?' Happy answers in the same thread.

Combines F084 Local privacy gate for documents: refuse bank statements and tax forms (text PDFs only)

Can be built because docs/nodes/media-understanding.md:10: OpenClaw documents reading inbound images, audio and video as a built-in step before the reply, and says the original media is still handed to the reply model.

How it works and its limits

How One switch: channels.imessage.includeAttachments: true. Photos then go to the reply model as images, and an attached PDF arrives as extracted text. The same deploy sets tools.media.audio.enabled: false, so audio understanding stays off until the voice card (F003) lists a transcriber on the Mac. In each parent's AGENTS.md the line that says Happy cannot see photos or files is replaced and a line says it cannot watch video; the smoke-eval check that forbids asking for an upload changes to match. A suggested layout for a flyer or form, to change after the first real ones: the dates, what to do, any money or form, the deadline, and which child if that matters; no line count. One planted-file test: a PDF and a photo with hidden instructions must cause no tool call, a hand-off to the web helper, a mail lookup, and a fetch or mail read by the parent's own agent included. One line goes on the printed sheet. No gate plugin; no house-rules rule.

Depends on G005: the printed sheet gains one line: no bank, tax or medical papers; Go-live check: the planted PDF and the planted photo cause no tool call (where the web helper F019 or the mail lookup G015 is live, a hand-off to it counts as a tool call). An attachment cannot reach an agent while the switch is off, so it runs on an eval-only copy where the endpoint takes the file, otherwise as one supervised turn from Tony's phone in the sitting the switch goes on; Go-live check: one live voice memo with audio understanding off is declined and no audio goes to the cloud model; Tony provides one supervised send of the planted PDF and the planted photo (made in the plan) from his own phone at execution

Limits

  • Nothing screens what a parent sends: any photo or PDF goes to the cloud model as it is. The only guard against a statement sent by mistake is the house rule on the printed sheet.
  • The same switch also lets voice memos and video in, and audio auto-detection tries a configured provider key before any local program, so audio understanding is set off in the same deploy and stays off until the voice card (F003) lists a transcriber on the Mac.
  • Happy cannot watch video on this provider set, so an AGENTS.md line has it say so and ask for a photo or a few screenshots.
  • store:false covers less than it reads: OpenAI can keep abuse-monitoring logs, content included, for up to 30 days unless the organisation has Zero Data Retention, and family photos fall under that. Tony accepted this on 12 Oct.
  • Medical papers are on the 'do not send' line, so the medical-bill reply layout is not built.
  • Only the switch is built: the optional pdf tool (page selection) is not part of this form.

Safety A photo or PDF is outside content read directly by the agent that holds a parent's chats. That agent replies only in its own chat. It is allowed the fetch tool and, where the lookup is on, the Gmail read tools, only so that its helpers can use them, and is told never to call them itself; reminders (F007), where live, are pinned to the asker in code. The hand-off to the web helper (F019), the roadmap's one remaining leak path, and a fetch or mail read by that agent itself have only prompt rules and the planted-file test until the house-rules plugin's check exists.

F003

Voice memos to Happy, transcribed on the Mac mini, with a spoken reply in the built-in Mac voice

Needs a buildMedium riskAdultsValue 2/5Effort MWave F

A parent sends a voice memo instead of typing; the Mac mini transcribes it, echoes the text back and answers, and the answer also arrives as an audio file in the built-in Mac voice. Speech is turned into text on the Mac mini, and the transcript then goes to the cloud model like any typed message. A parent can already dictate with the iPhone keyboard, so this is a convenience.

Example: A parent sends a voice memo: 'will it rain tomorrow morning?' Happy echoes the transcript, answers in text and attaches the same answer as audio. Or Tony sends /tts latest after a long answer and gets it read out.

Combines VOX-04 Spoken replies in a local voice (macOS say first, a neural voice later, cloud speech switched off)

Can be built because docs/nodes/audio.md:2: OpenClaw documents downloading and transcribing inbound voice notes and feeding the transcript into the reply, with local command-line transcribers among the options.

How it works and its limits

How In: an explicit tools.media.models CLI entry for whisper-cli (audio capability, {{AttachmentPath}}), with tools.media.audio.enabled: true and tools.media.audio.echoTranscript: true. It needs Homebrew whisper.cpp, ffmpeg and a GGML model file, installed from the admin account; OpenClaw converts the memo to WAV itself. With an explicit entry, auto-detection, which tries a configured provider key first, is not used. Out: the tts block with provider tts-local-cli running the macOS say command, tts.providers.microsoft.enabled: false and no cloud speech provider; tts.auto: "inbound" on the two parents' own agents only, so a voice memo gets a spoken answer as an audio file and every other agent stays text-only; /tts latest on demand, for Tony. The AGENTS.md line that says Happy cannot hear voice memos is replaced. First test: one live voice-memo turn whose trace shows the transcript, not the audio file, reaching the cloud model. No plugin; no rule in the house-rules plugin.

Depends on F002: attachment intake switched on (voice memos arrive through the same switch); whisper.cpp, ffmpeg and a GGML model file installed on the Mac mini from the admin account; First test, before it stays on: one live voice-memo turn whose trace shows that the transcript, and not the audio file, is what reaches the cloud model; Tony provides one test voice memo from his own phone at execution, and Jordan one from hers

Limits

  • A parent can already dictate a message with the iPhone keyboard and send it as text, so for the two adults this is a convenience and not a new ability.
  • Local-only is not the default in either direction: audio auto-detection tries a configured provider key before any local program, and the keyless Microsoft online voice is on by default and can serve as a fallback, so the transcriber is listed explicitly and the Microsoft voice is switched off. /tts provider <id> changes the provider for everyone, so having no cloud speech provider configured is the control, and the bundled sag skill (ElevenLabs, a cloud voice) stays off.
  • The reply is a plain audio file attachment (WAV, several megabytes for a few minutes), not a voice bubble; the voice-bubble option belongs to the Private API actions, which need SIP off.
  • Long replies are summarised by the cloud chat model before they are spoken, or cut short.
  • /tts latest and the other /tts commands work for Tony only: Jordan is not on the command list, and OpenClaw silently ignores /tts from her. The spoken reply after a voice memo does not depend on it.
  • Talk mode in the iPhone app (OCL-01) has its own speech setting and does not pick up this voice automatically.

Safety Speech is turned into text on the Mac mini; the transcript goes to the cloud model like any typed message, and the first live turn checks that the audio file is withheld. The spoken reply is made on the Mac, with the Microsoft voice off and no cloud speech provider. A voice memo comes from an allowlisted parent and brings no outside content.

  • Markdown pairs a whisper-cpp install with audio.preferredModel: "cli:whisper". The matcher compares that value with cli: plus the entry's exact command string (dist/resolve-KJuMET3H.mjs:148), so for whisper-cpp it must be cli:whisper-cli, or cli: plus the full path used in the entry; cli:whisper only matches the Python whisper CLI.
  • The Homebrew formula is now named whisper.cpp (formerly whisper-cpp) and its page says GGML model files are not downloaded by default. The 9 Oct note about a model that downloads automatically describes the Python whisper CLI (media-understanding.md:168), not whisper-cli.

Calendar and reminders 2

F007

Timed reminders over iMessage, one-off and repeating (Tony only)

Needs a buildMedium riskAdultsValue 4/5Effort MWave C

'Remind me at 4:30 to pick up the kids', or a repeating reminder, becomes a scheduled text to the asker, and reminders can be listed and cancelled; to change one, cancel it and set a new one. It works for Tony only: OpenClaw lets only a command owner use the scheduling tool from chat, and Jordan is not one, so she uses the Reminders app or Siri on her own phone.

Example: Tony texts: 'Remind me at 4:30 to pick up the kids.' At 4:30 he gets a text from Happy: 'Pick up the kids.' Later he texts 'what reminders do I have?' and then 'cancel the 4:30 one'.

Can be built because docs/automation/index.md:35: OpenClaw's automation guide names a timed reminder as a standard use of its built-in scheduler, as a one-shot job with exact timing.

How it works and its limits

How First T7, with cron.triggers.enabled: false already set: one throwaway reminder created from iMessage on a throwaway agent with no memory, accounts or other tools, removed in the same sitting. Then T5 for the scheduling tool: a logging plugin shows which fields the blocking check is given. Then the reminder rule in the house-rules plugin: add only, as a text to the asker, no web address, an empty tool list; list and remove allowed; update and run refused; blocked when the check itself fails. Then the roadmap's recipient test: five ways to change the recipient, the other parent included. Only then is the automations tool granted, to Tony's agent alone, in the agent's tool list and the sandbox's. One-shot reminders delete themselves after delivery; repeating ones carry the time zone. One instruction: when 'remind me' is unclear, ask. The smoke-eval case that expects 'I can't set reminders' is replaced by a reminder case.

Depends on G003 in its small form: cron.triggers.enabled: false, one of the three scheduler switches, set before any agent holds the scheduling tool; T7 passes first: a reminder can be created from an iMessage turn at all (not tried on this install); it runs on a throwaway agent that is removed in the same sitting; T5 for the scheduling tool: the blocking check is called for it and is given the job's target and tool list; The house-rules plugin with the reminder rule live before the scheduling tool is granted. This card creates the plugin if no earlier card has; when the plugin is first created, the roadmap's coded check on who may call the mail connector (G015) goes in as a rule too. Since 13 Oct that rule has two halves: no other person's agent may call a connector, and a parent's own agent may not itself call the tools it holds only for a helper (the Gmail read tools, the fetch tool). The second half needs T5 to show that the check is told which agent is calling; Tony provides the T7 text and one live reminder from his own phone at execution

Limits

  • For a plain personal timer, Siri and the iPhone Reminders app already do the job, including reminders tied to a place. Happy's version earns its place for reminders that come out of something Happy just read or answered, such as a flyer's dates (F010).
  • It works for Tony only: OpenClaw refuses the scheduling tool to a sender who is not a command owner, whatever the config says, and Tony is the only owner. Jordan uses the Reminders app or Siri on her own phone.
  • A reminder cannot be edited in place: the rule refuses any change to an existing job, so Tony cancels it and sets a new one.
  • Tony's agent can list every scheduled job on the gateway, Jordan's morning mail text included, and can remove one. The rule stops it changing or running them; a removal is written to the scheduler's admin log, and the job is then created again with the jobs script. Reminders are the one kind of job the jobs script does not create.
  • Once the shared Reminders list (F030) exists, 'remind me' can mean a text from Happy at a set time (this card) or an item on that list, so the agent is told to ask when it is unclear.
  • The card rests on T7, which has not been run: the installed docs describe creating a job from chat for Control UI administrators, not for an iMessage owner turn. If T7 fails, the rule and the grant are not built and Tony decides what comes next.

Safety OpenClaw advises keeping the scheduling tool off agents that read outside content, because it can name where a job's text goes, a web address included. Tony's agent gets it only after the reminder rule is live in code: add only, to the asker alone, no web address, an empty tool list, blocked when the check fails. Script triggers stay off.

Corrected since 9 Oct

  • Catalog JSON 'needs' lists --delete-after-run. One-shot --at jobs already delete themselves after confirmed delivery (how-it-works.md:19). The Markdown already says so.

Folded in

  • From G020 (Pending items view: approvals waiting, drafts unsent, watchers, reminders, open requests): Add the phrase 'what is pending?' to the reminders entry: it answers from the same automations list with every reminder and watcher and its next run time, and leaves gateway approvals out. Note that an owner's list shows every job on the gateway, not only that parent's; open requests (G010) and unanswered proposals join the list only if their tables are ever built.
  • From G009 (Family-only delivery: text the other parent or the parents' group, and ask-and-relay a yes or no, with the recipient pinned in code): The one check reminders need becomes the reminder rule in the house-rules plugin: a reminder may only be added, only as a text to the asker, with no web address and an empty tool list; listing and removing are allowed, and changing or running an existing job is refused. Both tools.message.crossContext switches stay off and no agent gets the message tool.
  • From F037 (Draft-only outreach texts (vendors, coaches, carpool parents)): Asking Happy to word a text to the plumber or the coach is ordinary chat that works today with nothing to build; what the item really records is the rule that Happy never sends to anyone outside the family, which the family delivery item (G009) already states. CRT-10 mentions it for a draft absence note, which still works without this item.

Not verified

  • The comparison with Siri and Apple Reminders for one-off personal timers was not sourced.

F009

Shared Google calendar, read-only: 'what's on Saturday?' and 'is Friday at 1 clear?'

Needs a buildMedium riskAdultsValue 4/5Effort MWave C

'What's on Saturday?' or 'is Friday at 1 clear?' is answered from the family's shared Google calendar, read-only; nothing on the calendar is changed. 'Clear' means nothing shows on the calendars the asking parent's own sign-in can see; the other parent's own calendars are not read, so Happy cannot say whether both parents are free. The same connection feeds the 21:00 evening text (F014).

Example: A parent texts: 'What's on Saturday?' and gets the day's events from the shared calendar. Tony asks 'is Friday at 1 clear?' and gets what his own sign-in shows for that hour; nothing on the calendar is changed.

Can be built because docs/concepts/delegate-architecture.md:48: OpenClaw describes read-only calendar access (read events, surface conflicts, summarize the day) as the lowest-risk tier of what an assistant agent does for the people it serves.

How it works and its limits

How One host-side stdio MCP server per parent. Sign-in: gog auth add <account> --services calendar --readonly, approved by that parent on Google's screen and stored apart from the mail sign-in, so the grant covers Calendar only. Server: gog --account <account> mcp --allow-tool calendar_events, because by default the server registers every read tool, mail and Drive search included. Each parent's own agent allows only its own calendar server's tool by name, in the agent's tool list and the sandbox's, and denies the other parent's; bundle-mcp is not opened. 'Is Friday at 1 clear?' is answered by listing that hour's events with the same tool; there is no free/busy tool. No rule of its own: the house-rules plugin's account-connector rule (a person's connector answers only that person's agents, blocked when the check fails) is live before the server is granted. One eval case: an event title that carries instructions must cause no tool call, a hand-off to the web helper included.

Depends on G015: gog installed and the Google sign-in app published, both set up with mail and reused here (a sign-in from an app left in Testing status expires after seven days; T1's day-8 check is run with mail); The house-rules plugin with its account-connector rule live before the calendar server is granted. Timed reminders (F007) are expected to create the plugin; if this card comes first, it creates the plugin with that rule; Each parent approves a calendar-only, read-only sign-in on Google's own screen at execution; Jordan approves her own; T2, calendar half, before go-live: the calendar sign-in cannot run a mail search, and each parent's agent shows exactly one calendar tool and is refused the other parent's; The connector's gate from wave A (gog may reach Google and nothing else: the blocking rule and the local proxy's list of hosts) checked to cover the calendar server; Tony provides the Google account each parent signs in with, and the name of the shared calendar, at execution

Limits

  • 'Is Friday at 1 clear?' is answered only from events the asking parent's sign-in can see: the shared calendar, and that parent's own calendars unless the tool can be pinned to one calendar. 'Clear' does not mean both parents are free. gog's server offers one calendar tool, the events list, and no free/busy tool; reading each parent's own calendar as busy-only belongs to the conflict watch (MKT-06).
  • Happy does not write to the calendar. A date from a flyer or an email is in calendar answers, and in the evening text, only after a parent adds the event on the phone.
  • A renewal, expiry or upkeep date is one calendar event with an alert that a parent types once on the shared calendar (a repeating event for upkeep). It then shows in calendar answers and the evening text, and the phone's own alert works when Happy is down. There is no renewals table and no monthly 'coming due' text.
  • A public feed (the school district's calendar, a team schedule, library events) shows up in calendar answers only after the shared Google calendar is subscribed to its link, which Google allows from a computer browser only; Google gives no refresh interval, and TeamSnap says changes can take up to 24 hours to appear.
  • Two layers keep one parent's calendar out of the other parent's agent: tool permissions with an explicit deny (checked by T2), and the coded account-connector rule. Tony accepted going without the second layer for mail only, so here it is in place first. If T5 shows the blocking check is never called for a connector's tools, the rule cannot be written and Tony decides whether one layer is enough for the calendar too.

Safety Read-only and calendar-only: each sign-in covers Calendar alone, apart from the mail sign-in; the server offers only the events tool, to its owner's agent alone, held there by tool permissions and the coded connector rule. Outsiders can write event titles, so calendar text is outside content; that agent is told not to fetch pages itself (it holds the fetch tool only for the web helper, and the house-rules rule blocks it if T5 allows that rule), and its one way out is the hand-off to the web helper (F019).

Corrected since 9 Oct

  • The 9 Oct wording has Tony hand-write the calendar MCP server. gogcli.sh/mcp.html documents a built-in stdio server (gog --account <account> mcp) with a read-only calendar_events tool and an --allow-tool filter, so listing events needs no custom code. Freebusy and conflicts exist only as CLI commands (gogcli.sh/commands) and still need a wrapper.
  • Catalog JSON 'needs' expects a calendar.readonly scope from --services calendar. The documented switch is --readonly on gog auth add; Google's scope list does include calendar.readonly (developers.google.com/workspace/calendar/api/auth). The Markdown asked to verify the flag; gog's command page confirms it.

Folded in

Still to move across: G012's Google Help and TeamSnap sources. If a change alert is wanted for the district calendar too, widen SRC-09's wording from sports feeds to any public feed.
  • From F063 (Renewals, expiry and upkeep look-ahead (passports, licences, car, domains, filed documents, check-ups, home and car upkeep)): One line on the calendar card: a renewal, expiry or upkeep date is one calendar event with an alert that a parent adds once to the shared Google calendar (a repeating event for upkeep); the event's own alert gives the notice and works when Happy is down. The event then shows in calendar answers and, the evening before, in the 21:00 evening text; Tony can also ask Happy for a timed reminder (F007). Happy does not add the event itself.
  • From F012 (Birthday, anniversary and gift-date heads-up): The phones already do the core of this: birthdays saved in contacts appear in the calendar by themselves, and the iPhone calendar can alert up to a week ahead. What is left (anniversary and gift dates with last year's gift note) is a few more rows in the dated-reminders list (F063), not a separate daily job with its own hand-entered table. Nothing depends on it.

  • Whether the blocking check is called for a connector's tools at all, and which fields it is given (T5).
  • Whether gog's calendar_events tool can be pinned to a single calendar id was not confirmed.
  • That events from a URL-subscribed calendar are returned through the Google Calendar API, and so through gog, was not confirmed.
  • Whether the school district, clubs and library the family uses publish feed links was not checked.

Web reading and research 1

F019

Research helper: answers from public web pages with the link and the time fetched

Needs a buildMedium riskAdultsValue 5/5Effort LWave B

Happy can read public web pages that load without JavaScript or a login: a research helper with no memory, no accounts and no family data fetches the page, and the parent's own agent relays the answer with its link and the time it was fetched. When a page cannot be read, Happy says 'could not verify'. Nothing the helper fetches can reach the home network.

Example: A parent texts: 'What time does the town pool open on Saturday? Check their site.' Happy sends the hours with the link and when the page was fetched.

Combines WEB-01 Web egress guardrails for fetch and browser (no LAN, no headers, no fallback provider); F022 Citation and freshness rules; G014 Long-running task etiquette: acknowledge, background, notify, cancel

Can be built because docs/tools/web-fetch.md:11: OpenClaw's built-in page fetcher gets a URL and returns its readable text, which is what lets the helper answer from a public page.

How it works and its limits

How First T4: one hand-off from Tony's agent to the helper, with a time limit, must return its answer in the same chat while agents still cannot see each other's sessions. Agent: a shared research agent from the family file: a fresh sandbox per conversation, memory search off, no accounts, web_search and web_fetch only, its own capped key. Each parent's agent adds research to its subagents.allowAgents, beside its own mail reader; sessions_spawn and subagents.requireAgentId: true are already set by the mail lookup, or are set here if the lookup is off; the time limit is the gateway-wide agents.defaults.subagents.runTimeoutSeconds, because 2026.9.7 rejects that key under one agent. Under the pattern Tony said on 13 Oct he expects to adopt for every helper, each parent's agent is also allowed web_fetch, which it is denied today (in its tool list and its sandbox tool list): on 2026.9.7 an agent started by another keeps only the tools its asker is allowed (the asker's allowed tools and its denies are passed to the helper and applied last), so the helper could not fetch otherwise. The helper's own list, web_search and web_fetch, is what narrows the hand-off. Guardrails: both dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork keys unset, tools.web.fetch.headers empty, no fetch-provider plugin, tools.web.fetch.useTrustedEnvProxy off, browser.enabled: false, browser.evaluateEnabled: false. One rule in the helper's AGENTS.md: give the link and the time fetched, show the page's own date when it has one, give a price or date only from a fetched page, say 'could not verify'. In each parent's AGENTS.md the 'cannot open links' line becomes the hand-off rule: never fetch a page yourself, hand it to the helper, and what a task may carry; its smoke-eval case changes too. Four planted eval cases; in each, a fetch by the parent's own agent counts as a failure. Tony's agent first, Jordan's a day later. No plugin and no house-rules rule in this wave; when the house-rules plugin is created in wave C (planned there by Tony's choice of 13 Oct to keep the wave order), its who-may-call rule also covers web_fetch on a parent's own agent, if test T5 shows that the check is told which agent is calling; otherwise an instruction and the tool-call record stay the only guard.

Depends on The outbound gate, built first in the same plan (Tony's answer 7b; the roadmap's gate before web reading): the firewall blocking every program by default with one rule per program, and the outbound proxy for the gateway's calls enforcing after at least one night in report mode; the plugin allowlist left open at the M1 sign-off is closed in the same step. No other card carries this work, so its hours are counted on this card; T4 passes first: a hand-off from a parent's agent returns the helper's answer with agent-to-agent messaging off and session visibility set to self (the roadmap lists this as not yet confirmed); Four planted eval cases pass before go-live: a home-network address, a public address that redirects to one, a public name that resolves to one, and a result that asks the parent's agent to pass its notes to the helper; If the mail lookup (G015) is live: its seeded-mail test is run again with the helper present; Tony provides a new capped model key for the helper at execution

Limits

  • The plain fetch runs no JavaScript and cannot log in, so such pages stay unread until the extra readers (F020) exist, and Happy says 'could not verify'. A slow lookup gets no 'on it' and no plain-words 'cancel that': the helper's built-in finish report is the only progress message, and a lookup ends at its time limit or at Tony's built-in stop.
  • If the hand-off test (T4) fails, the only documented alternative is session visibility tree for the whole gateway, which changes a signed-off setting and needs Tony's yes plus a re-run of the separation check.
  • The home-network block rests on the fetch tool resolving and pinning the address itself, so tools.web.fetch.useTrustedEnvProxy stays off and both private-network keys stay truly unset: an explicitly written false on the browser key turns hostname navigation into an allowlist and would stop the later research browser (F020).
  • Once the helper can fetch pages, neither the firewall nor the proxy can hold the gateway program to a list of hosts; they refuse home-network addresses and nothing more, so tool permissions, not the firewall, keep the mail readers and the shared agents off the web; a parent's own agent is allowed the fetch tool so that the helper can use it, and there an instruction and the planted tests do that work.
  • The answer rule and the rule on what goes into a task (the town and the children's ages yes, names and the school no) are prompt rules; nothing mechanical enforces them, and the planted eval cases are the only check. The roadmap's prompt-injection tripwire is not built with this card: by Tony's answer of 12 Oct it waits for local models.
  • The fetch tool's home-network check covers web_fetch only, so host-side helpers that take a web address (the summarize wrapper, watcher scripts) need their own scheme, host and resolved-address checks.

Safety The helper reads untrusted pages but holds no memory, accounts or family data, and cannot reach the home network. The roadmap's one remaining leak path stays open: a parent's agent holds private chats and writes the task text for a helper that can fetch any public address. A prompt rule and planted tests guard it; the helper's answer is treated as untrusted. Under that pattern the path is one step shorter: the parent's own agent is itself allowed the fetch tool, because a helper keeps only the tools its asker is allowed, and only its instructions and the planted tests keep it from fetching a page itself until the house-rules plugin's check exists in wave C, and after that only if test T5 allowed it.

Lists and household data 2

F030

Shared Apple Reminders list: Happy reads it, adds to it and ticks items off

Needs a buildMedium riskAdultsValue 4/5Effort MWave G

Happy can read, add to and tick off items on the Apple Reminders list the two parents share, so a change shows up on both phones. Tony names the list at execution. Nothing is coded until a by-hand test shows that an item added from the Mac reaches that list on both phones.

Example: After Happy answers 'what do I need for pancakes for six?', a parent texts 'add the flour, eggs and buttermilk to our list'. The three items appear on the shared list on both parents' phones. Later the other parent texts 'what's still on the list?' and gets the open items.

Can be built because skills/apple-reminders/SKILL.md:37: OpenClaw ships a skill for listing, adding and completing Apple Reminders from the Mac, meant for people who want the tasks to appear in the Reminders app on their phones.

How it works and its limits

How First T9, by hand, before any code: in happy's desktop session join the list Tony names, add and tick off one item with remindctl, and look at both phones; then add one item with a due time and note whether a phone alerts. If the item does not arrive, try a list that Happy's account owns and shares to both parents; if that fails too, the card is dropped. Then an in-house host-side tool plugin wrapping remindctl with three verbs (list, add, complete) on that one list only, no delete and no due dates, allowed on both parents' own agents in the agent's tool list and the sandbox's. Reminders access is granted once by hand in the gateway's own process context. One instruction: when 'remind me' could mean a timed text or a list item, ask. No house-rules rule: the tool's three verbs and its one list, fixed in its configuration, are the limit in code.

Depends on Tony provides the name of the shared Reminders list at execution, and confirms that it is shared with the two parents only; happy's Apple Account invited to that list from a parent's phone, with iCloud Reminders on; remindctl installed on the Mac mini and Reminders access granted in the gateway's own process context; T9 passes by hand before any plugin code: an item added from the Mac appears on the list on both phones

Limits

  • For a single item spoken to the phone, Siri already creates reminders with nothing to build. The bridge earns its place when the items come out of something Happy read or planned (a recipe link, the dinner plan in F033, a flyer).
  • If T9 fails for a list a parent owns, the fallback is a list that Happy's account owns and shares to both parents; if that fails too, the card is dropped.
  • The tool sets no due dates and cannot delete: an item added by mistake is ticked off, or removed on the phone. T9 notes whether a due time alerts a phone, in case a parent later asks for dated items.
  • Who sees the list is set in Apple's sharing, not in Happy's code. What one parent's agent adds is seen by the other parent, and by anyone else the list is ever shared with.
  • A shared Apple Note as a second filing target is not part of this build.
  • A scheduled text of the open list is not built; if a parent asks for one and names the day and hour, it is one more job in the jobs script.

Safety The tool can only list, add and complete on the one list fixed in its configuration; the model cannot write elsewhere or delete. An added item shows on every phone the list is shared with, and Happy's code cannot check the sharing, so Tony confirms at execution that only the two parents share it. List text typed by anyone on the list is outside content.

Folded in

  • From OCL-08 (Notes and task apps as a filing target (Apple Notes, Obsidian, Things, Bear, Notion, Trello)): Carry one caveat into F030: a shared Apple Note could later be a second filing target using the same host-side wrapper, but only after an unattended append is proven. Things, Bear, Notion and Trello are not pursued, and the F043 vault folder can be opened in Obsidian by a person with no agent tool.
  • From F032 (Grocery and errand capture by text or voice, plus Saturday shop list): Give F030 the example 'add oat milk' and one optional Saturday-morning job per parent that texts the open shopping list. Note that Reminders exposes no purchase history, so 'not bought in three weeks' is out, and that capture by voice memo waits on local transcription (F003).

Not verified

  • No opened source confirms that remindctl can add to or complete items on a shared iCloud list owned by another family member; its README only says reminders sync through the normal iCloud path (T9).
  • Which binary macOS records the Reminders permission against when the launchd gateway spawns remindctl is not documented in any opened source; it needs one test on happy's logged-in desktop.
  • Whether a due time on an item added from the Mac alerts a parent's phone on a shared list (the second half of T9).

F031

Household database: shared rows for the dose log and the coverage planner

Needs a buildMedium riskAdults and kidsValue 4/5Effort SWave E

A small database on the Mac mini that both parents' agents read and write, so either parent gets the same answer whoever entered the row. It is built only as far as two planned features need it: one table for the sick-day dose log (CRT-10) and one for the childcare coverage grid (CRT-11). It has no general 'save a fact' tools: reference text both parents look up lives in the family handbook (F043), and each parent's own notes stay with that parent (F041).

Example: One parent texts Happy what they gave the kindergartner and when. Later the other parent asks 'when was the last dose logged?' and gets the same row, with who logged it. In the same way, one parent texts that a no-school week is covered, and the other parent's 'which weeks are still open?' no longer lists it.

Backed by Maintenance Checklist | ENERGY STAR energystar.gov: A US government energy programme tells households to inspect, clean or change heating and cooling filters every month and to book yearly pre-season check-ups, the kind of dated upkeep schedule this store keeps for both parents; opened again in this round.

How it works and its limits

How One in-house tool plugin over Node's built-in node:sqlite, with one database file on the Mac mini. It sits in the config repo's plugins/ folder like the weather plugin: the ordinary deploy copies it and it loads from plugins.load.paths after a restart. No general tools: no schedule tools and no fact_get or fact_set. Each feature adds one table and its own typed tools: the dose log (CRT-10) and the coverage grid (CRT-11). Every input is typed and short in the tool's own schema (a date or time, a whole number, a choice from a fixed list, a label of at most about 40 characters); no separate secret detector. The tools are allowed by name on the two parents' own agents (tools.alsoAllow and the sandbox gate tools.sandbox.tools) and on no shared agent or mail reader. A scheduled job that reads a table lists the tool by the name the plugin declares. No house-rules rule is added.

Depends on No other planned card is needed first. It is built in the same plan as its first user, the dose log (CRT-10) or the coverage planner (CRT-11), whichever comes first; the other adds its own table when it is built; Node's built-in SQLite module on the installed Node, so no new package; The config repo's plugins folder and the ordinary deploy with a gateway restart, the way the weather plugin is deployed, plus one more path in plugins.load.paths

Limits

  • Everything in it is shared between the two adults on purpose: neither table filters by person. That steps outside 'one data domain per person', by Tony's pick of the two features on 12 Oct. Something meant for one parent belongs in that parent's own notes (F041).
  • Only two tables are planned. There is no general upkeep or 'when is the filter due?' table: a repeating date is a calendar event or a reminder.
  • A later feature that needs rows both parents' agents write adds its own table and typed tools here; it does not start a second store.
  • Inputs are short and typed, with no secret detector, so a short secret typed as a label would be stored; the standing instruction never to ask for or reveal passwords, keys or codes is the only guard against that.
  • The dose table holds what was given to a child, and that text goes to the cloud model whenever a parent's agent reads it back. Tony picked the dose log knowing this, and its card (CRT-10) carries his confirm step at execution.
  • The rows can be read only through Happy: when the Mac mini or the cloud model is down, neither parent can get at them.

Safety Both parents' agents read and write the same rows, so the store is shared between the two adults on purpose. Its tools are allowed by name on those two agents only. The tool's own schema keeps every input short and typed, which leaves a planted instruction little room to persist. No send and no web access is added.

The parents' own eval-only copies are generated with the same tool list as the parents' agents, so what a test run may write into the real file is settled then.

Memory, knowledge and skills 3

F041

Saved notes: 'remember this' goes to that parent's own notes and is found again by keyword

Needs a buildMedium riskAdultsValue 5/5Effort MWave C

A parent texts 'remember that...' and their own agent saves the line to that parent's own notes and says what it saved. In a later chat the note is found by searching for its words; it is not in view at the start of a chat, and Happy saves nothing a parent did not ask it to save. Each parent's notes stay with that parent: the other parent's agent cannot find them.

Example: A parent texts: 'Remember that the library books are due back on the 20th.' A week later, in a new chat, the same parent asks 'when are the library books due?' and Happy finds the note and answers. The other parent's agent cannot find it.

Combines F046 Semantic memory search with local embeddings (text only)

Can be built because docs/concepts/memory.md:31: OpenClaw's memory guide presents asking the agent to remember a fact, which it then writes to its memory files, as the normal way to use memory.

How it works and its limits

How T6 runs first, on Tony's eval-only copy. Then the generator gives each parent's agent write and edit (also in the sandbox tool gate), with apply_patch denied by name and read left denied, plus memory_search and memory_get, keyword-only (memory.search.provider: "none", already set). The sandbox stays closed to the agent folder (workspaceAccess: "none"), so a note lands in a notes folder inside the agent's own sandbox workspace; that folder is added to that agent's own search paths (agents.entries.<id>.memory.search.extraPaths, never the global list). Instructions: save only what the parent asked, in the parent's words; say what was saved; do not save a child's health details. Not built: a read-write workspace, tracking of web tool calls, the session-memory hook, any copy of notes outside the agent, search by meaning. House-rules plugin: no rule when T6 passes. The separation canaries are extended to memory search.

Depends on A generator change in happy-config: write, edit, memory_search and memory_get allowed on each parent's own agent and in its sandbox tool gate, with apply_patch denied by name; The line in each parent's agent instructions that says Happy cannot write files is reworded for notes; Tony provides at execution: one harmless fact saved from his phone and one from Jordan's phone, for the two-day recall test

Limits

  • A saved note is found only when the agent searches for it: it is not in view at the start of a chat, and a scheduled text or a hand-off to a helper does not know it.
  • Notes are found by their words, not their meaning, so a question worded differently from the note may miss it. Search by meaning (an embedding model on the Mac mini, a deliverable of the roadmap's local-models milestone, which Tony has put off) and OpenClaw's Active Memory recall stay later options that are Tony's call; neither is part of this build.
  • Notes belong to one parent. A fact both parents should get the same answer to goes into the family file (F042) or the family handbook (F043), both typed by Tony.
  • No refusal is built for a 'remember' in a turn that also carried web results. OpenClaw is expected to label such a note untrusted by itself, T6 records what actually happens, and a prompt rule plus a behaviour test are what stand against a planted 'remember this'.
  • There is no undo and no copy of note text anywhere else. A parent asks 'what did you save about me?' to read their notes back; the weekly text (G006) only lists which note files changed.
  • The design rests on T6, which has not been run, and it has to pass for Jordan as she is, a non-owner. If it fails for her, notes go live for Tony first while a fix is found. If it fails outright, the fallback left is the original design (a read-write agent folder plus one house-rules rule that keeps writes inside the notes folder), which reverses two signed-off settings; Tony says yes or no to it at execution.

Safety Notes stay in the parent's own agent. The write tools reach only that agent's own sandbox folder, so they cannot change its rules file or the rendered family facts; shared agents and mail readers have no memory search. A note is where a planted instruction could persist, so a planted 'remember this' must save nothing in five runs of five.

Corrected since 9 Oct

F042

Family facts from the family file, known to each parent's agent in every chat

Needs a buildMedium riskAdultsValue 4/5Effort SWave C

Tony types the family facts he wants Happy to know into the family file: to start with, the two children, their school years and the school district. After the next deploy both parents' agents begin every one-to-one chat already knowing them, so nobody has to explain who 'the third-grader' is. The facts are not rendered into the web helper, the mail readers or any shared agent.

Example: In a fresh chat a parent texts: 'write a two-line absence note for our third-grader for Friday.' Happy drafts it with the child's first name and the school district, which nobody typed in that chat, and the parent sends it themselves.

Combines G011 Bilingual replies and grandparent-facing translations

Can be built because docs/concepts/user-model.md:12: OpenClaw documents USER.md as the place for stable preferences, relationships and context, loaded beside MEMORY.md at session start to guide later chats.

How it works and its limits

How One generator step. New fields in family.json5 hold the facts Tony types; gen-family.mjs renders them through new template placeholders into files it already writes for each parent's own agent: USER.md while they fit under its 4,000-character cap, otherwise a section of AGENTS.md. The generator does not start writing MEMORY.md, which stays with OpenClaw and the eval marker (the deploy script never touches it), and no trigger comments are used. Nothing is rendered into the bootstrap files of the web helper, the mail readers or any shared agent; a scheduled job that needs a fact carries it in its own message. No reply-language line is rendered. No tool, no send path and no house-rules rule is added. Once the web helper (F019) exists, its hand-off canary is run with the real facts present.

Depends on family.json5 and the gen-family generator in happy-config: new fields, new template placeholders and a few lines in the generator (today it renders four files per person, with the person's name and the home town and no other fact); Tony provides at execution: the two children's first names, their school years and the school district's name, entered into the family file and nowhere else, and any routine or standing preference he wants known

Limits

  • USER.md has a 4,000-character cap that everything rendered into it shares, so the list has to stay short; what does not fit goes into a section of AGENTS.md and takes prompt space in every session of that parent's agent.
  • Rendered facts change only when Tony edits the family file and redeploys; a parent cannot change one by text. What a parent tells Happy in chat goes to that parent's own saved notes (F041).
  • The typed facts, the children's names and school among them, are sent to the cloud model at the start of every chat of each parent's own agent.
  • Children's health details are not typed into the family file: that is the default Tony kept, and the dose log (CRT-10) is the one planned feature that holds any.
  • Each parent's agent can search the web today. The default Tony kept (a search may use the town and the children's ages, never their names or the school) is a prompt rule, not an enforced limit.
  • Whether a scheduled run loads the rendered file has not been tried on a live job, so a scheduled text that needs a fact carries it in its own message.

Safety The rendered files go only into the two parents' own agents, never into the web helper, a mail reader or a shared agent. They hold the children's names and school and go to the cloud model with every chat; children's health details stay out. No tool or send path is added, and the hand-off canary is re-run with real facts present.

F043

Family handbook: shared pages Tony types that both parents' agents can search

Needs a buildMedium riskAdultsValue 4/5Effort SWave E

One shared family handbook that both parents' agents can search: plain pages Tony types, such as appliance details and who services what, plus the reference pages other planned cards read. Either parent asks and gets the same stored answer. Happy does not write or change pages; a parent who wants something added tells Tony.

Example: Made up to show the feature: suppose Tony has typed a page listing appliance model numbers and repair contacts. Jordan asks 'who do we call about the dishwasher?' and gets the contact from that page; Tony would get the same answer.

Combines F034 Home systems and service-provider registry with lookup

Can be built because docs/plugins/memory-wiki.md:11: OpenClaw bundles a plugin whose stated job is to turn lasting knowledge into a maintained, searchable wiki that sits beside the agent's ordinary memory.

How it works and its limits

How One shared Markdown folder on the Mac mini, outside both parents' workspaces. Tony types the pages in the config repo, and the ordinary deploy, which already copies Markdown files under its shared folder, puts them in place. The generator adds the folder to each parent's own agent (agents.entries.<id>.memory.search.extraPaths, never the global list); the agents find pages with memory_search and memory_get, keyword-only (memory.search.provider: "none", already set). No agent gets a tool that writes to the folder, and shared agents and the mail readers keep memory search off. Not built: the memory-wiki plugin and its four tools, saving a page from a photo, manuals by link. The shared-folder part of T6 runs first, on an eval-only copy. No house-rules rule is needed.

Depends on F041 saved notes, which grants the two search tools (memory_search and memory_get, keyword-only) to each parent's agent; a plan that builds this card before F041 grants them here, about half an hour more; Tony provides at execution: the first pages, typed by him (which page comes first is his choice)

Limits

  • Only Tony adds or changes a page, by typing or pasting it and deploying; that includes a page another planned card produces, such as the emergency page of CRT-13. A parent cannot save a page by text or by sending a photo.
  • Pages are found by their words when the agent searches; they are not in view at the start of a chat, and a scheduled text or a hand-off to a helper does not know them.
  • The folder is shared on purpose, which steps outside 'one data domain per person' by Tony's choice of 12 Oct. It holds household reference only: no copy of either parent's own notes, and by the default he kept, no child's health details.
  • The text of a page goes to the cloud model whenever a search returns it.
  • A date that needs a reminder does not belong here: it is a calendar event or a reminder.
  • The card rests on a search that has not been tried. If a sandboxed agent cannot find pages in a shared folder, the few facts go into the rendered family facts (F042) instead of a searched folder.

Safety Shared between the two adults on purpose, for household reference only. No agent can write a page: only Tony does, through the reviewed deploy, so a planted instruction cannot be saved into it from a chat. The folder is added to the two parents' agents alone; shared agents and mail readers keep memory search off. No send path is added.

Not verified

  • The installed code labels files indexed from outside an agent's workspace as untrusted origin (dist/memory-path-provenance-BiFQlpIk.mjs:32); whether that hides handbook pages or brings them back with a warning label was not tested.
  • That the same folder listed as an extra path on two agents is indexed for both and for no other agent: the multi-agent page describes a shared extra-path folder for reference material; not tried here.
  • That the deploy's existing copy step for shared Markdown files is a workable home for the pages: read in the deploy script, not tried with a handbook folder.

Mail access 2

G015

Read-only Gmail for each parent: a 07:00 weekday mail text and 'did I get an email about X?'

Needs a buildMedium riskAdultsValue 4/5Effort LWave A

Each parent approves read-only access to their own Gmail once, on Google's own screen; the token stays on the Mac mini, Happy never holds a password, and nothing in Gmail is changed, labelled, drafted or sent. Each weekday at 07:00 Eastern a locked-down mail reader texts its owner a short list of what needs a reply, has a deadline or involves money, with the school lines first and no links. A parent can also ask 'did I get an email about X?' and get the sender, the date and the gist from their own inbox.

Example: 07:00, text to Tony: 'Mail. School: a form for the third-grader is due back on Friday 16 October. Needs you: the plumber asks you to confirm Thursday's visit by tomorrow; a bill is due on Tuesday 20 October.' Later Jordan texts her own Happy 'did I get an email about class photo day?' and gets the sender, the date and one line of gist from her own inbox.

Combines F047 Per-person read-only Gmail (<p>-gmail MCP); F016 07:00 morning email digest with action items (M4)

Backed by Connect the Google Workspace app to Gemini Apps - Gemini Apps Help support.google.com: Google's own assistant offers consumers summaries and quick answers drawn from their Gmail, the same read-only lookup this gives each adult's mail agent; opened again in this round.

How it works and its limits

How Connector: gog mcp, gog's own MCP server, as one host-side stdio entry under mcp.servers per parent, started with only that parent's token and narrowed with --allow-tool to the Gmail read tools; a read-only token each from gog auth add (--services Gmail only, --gmail-scope readonly). Reader: one generated <p>-mail agent per parent: profile: "minimal", only <p>-gmail__* allowed (also in tools.sandbox.tools) and denied by name elsewhere, except on that parent's own agent once its lookup is on (see Lookup); memory search off; one cloud model, storage off, no fallback. Gate: the connector reaches Google and nothing else. The wave A runbook found that a firewall rule cannot name Google's hosts for this program, so it builds the gate as one firewall rule that blocks every direct connection by the connector plus a small local proxy that lets it reach three named Google hosts; Tony's yes to that is asked at the runbook's step A4. Text: one weekday 07:00 Eastern job per reader from the jobs script (G003), Gmail read tools only, delivered to its owner: own label, school lines first (F051), no links, medical mail by sender and subject only, silent on an empty morning. Lookup (Tony, 13 Oct): <p>-main hands a mail question to its own <p>-mail through subagents.allowAgents, with subagents.requireAgentId: true (the list governs only a call that names an agent; a call that names none would start a copy of the asking agent), with a two-minute default time limit. On 2026.9.7 an agent started by another keeps only the tools its asker is allowed (the asker's allowed tools and its denies are passed to the helper and applied last), so <p>-main is itself allowed the three <p>-gmail read tools (also in its sandbox tool list) and no longer denies that one server; its instructions tell it to hand every mail question to the reader and never to call those tools itself. The reader's own list, the three read tools and nothing else, is what narrows the hand-off. Eval-only copies of a parent's agent never hold a connector tool or the hand-off to a mail reader (except T5's throwaway pair in wave C, which reads only the test mailbox), so the lookup is tested live. House rules: adds the account-connector rule when that plugin is first created. From then the parent's own agent is blocked in code from calling the Gmail tools it holds, if test T5 shows that the check is told which agent is calling.

Depends on G003 in its small form: the three scheduler switches and the short jobs script, which creates each 07:00 job with its owner's handle read from the family file. The job is made by that script, not by the scheduling tool, so Jordan's copy needs no command-owner right; gog installed at a pinned version, with its read-only, service and tool-filter options confirmed on the installed program; A Google Cloud project, sign-in client and consent screen published to In production: Tony sets these up by hand at execution; Each parent's own approval of read-only Gmail on Google's screen: Tony first, then Jordan, who has agreed; One firewall rule: the mail connector may reach Google and nothing else. Tony accepted on 12 Oct that mail is read with this one rule before the full firewall and the outbound proxy exist. The wave A runbook builds the gate as one blocking rule plus a small local proxy for the connector, because a firewall rule cannot name Google's hosts for this program; his yes to that is asked at its step A4; Tony provides at execution: a second Google account used only as a test mailbox for planted mail, and a capped model key for each mail reader; Tony provides at execution: the school senders' addresses, used as a hint in the job's message for the school lines (F051), not as a filter; The Zero Data Retention application to OpenAI filed and its date written down; mail does not wait for the answer (Tony, 12 Oct)

Limits

  • The read-only grant lets the connector read every message in the account. The school lines are picked out by the model, with no sender filter and no check, so it may miss a school mail or list one that is not; and mail that arrives during the day waits for the next morning's text.
  • Mail text goes to the cloud model on Tony's go-ahead of 12 Oct, and is read before the full firewall and the outbound proxy exist. Until OpenAI approves Zero Data Retention its abuse-monitoring log can keep that text for up to 30 days. Both points depart from the roadmap's rules for mail readers, by his choice.
  • Nothing about the connector has been tried on this Mac: gog is not installed, so its flags come from upstream docs, and whether a token from the published sign-in app outlives seven days on a personal account is test T1. If the day-8 search fails, the choice is a weekly sign-in per parent or a different connector.
  • 'No links' and 'sender and subject only for medical mail' are instructions to the reader, not enforced limits. What limits harm is that the reader holds only Gmail read tools and its outputs are the scheduled text to its owner and, once the lookup is on, its answer to its owner's own agent.
  • The lookup goes two steps beyond the roadmap's mail design. Its answer comes back into the parent's own agent, which holds that parent's chats, can search the web and will later hand tasks to the web helper. And by Tony's decision of 13 Oct that agent is itself allowed the Gmail read tools, because a helper keeps only the tools its asker is allowed: an instruction, checked by a count of its tool calls, keeps it from reading mail itself, not a tool limit, until the house-rules plugin's check exists, and then only if test T5 allows that check. Only prompt rules and a seeded-mail test stand between them, so it goes live in its own step and can be switched off without touching the morning text.
  • Google's Gemini app already answers questions from a person's own Gmail and lists a daily digest among its scheduled actions; Happy adds only asking, and being told, in the iMessage thread.
  • With the lookup on, each mail question also leaves the reader's transcript of that hand-off on the Mac (archived an hour after it finishes and kept until the disk budget evicts it, unless the optional 30-day setting of the wave A runbook is switched on) and the answer in the parent's own chat transcript.

Safety Each reader holds private mail and reads outsiders' text, so it has no way out: only Gmail read tools, and two outputs: the scheduled text, which the jobs script addresses from the family file, and, once the lookup is on, its answer to its owner's own agent. One reader, connector and token per parent; the two parents are held apart by tool permissions, an explicit deny and two tests until the house-rules plugin exists. The lookup is the weaker half: once it is on, the parent's own agent is allowed the same three read tools so that the reader it starts can use them, and only its instructions and a count of its tool calls keep it from reading mail itself.

The minimal profile does not allow MCP tools implicitly either (same file, lines 36 and 41).

F049

Email me this: a long answer sent to the asker's own inbox

Needs a buildMedium riskAdultsValue 3/5Effort MWave G

A parent texts 'email me this' and the long answer, table or plan lands in that parent's own inbox as plain text; either parent can ask. It is sent from the Gmail address Happy already has unless Tony names another. The only address the send tool accepts is the asker's own: a check in code blocks every other send, and blocks when the check itself fails.

Example: Jordan texts: 'Email me that comparison.' The full text arrives in her own inbox as plain text from Happy's address. A send that names anyone else on the To, cc or bcc line, or that goes out as a reply-all, is blocked.

Backed by Top features you can try on Alexa+ (About Amazon) aboutamazon.com: Amazon's own feature list says a user can ask Alexa+ to recap a conversation and send the recap to the Alexa app or to their own email, the same 'email me this' step for an assistant's answer.

How it works and its limits

How One shared mail-out server on the host: gog run as an MCP server for the sending address with its write and Gmail-send flags and only gmail_send_message registered, signed in with a send-only grant if the installed gog offers one. It is allowed by name on each parent's own agent, denied on the mail readers and every shared agent, and sits behind the same gate as the mail readers' connector (wave A's blocking rule and the local proxy's Google hosts). The card adds one rule to the house-rules plugin, the send-to-owner rule: a send is blocked unless the caller is a parent's own agent and the one recipient is that agent's owner, read from the family file, with no cc, bcc, reply or reply-all target, send-as alias or HTML body. The check fails closed. Before go-live: T5's send-tool turn, then the roadmap's five seeded ways to change the recipient (the other parent and a reply-all among them) and an injected web page. No send cap.

Depends on G015 mail reading live first: gog installed on the Mac mini and the published Google sign-in app, whose tokens T1 shows to last past seven days; this card reuses both; The house-rules plugin: this card adds its send-to-owner rule, and creates the plugin itself if no earlier card has (timed reminders, F007, is the likely first); whichever card creates it also puts in the account-connector rule (G015); The outbound gate that is built before web reading (the gate F019 waits for): the firewall blocking every program by default and the outbound proxy; the roadmap puts the send-to-owner test in that same gate; A send-only Google sign-in for the sending address, approved by Tony in a browser at execution; Tony provides the sending address at execution (default: the Gmail address Happy already has; no new account is created); Tony provides each parent's own receiving address for the family file at execution (default: the Gmail address that parent connected for mail reading)

Limits

  • The promise that nobody else can be a recipient rests on one in-house rule, and it is not yet shown that the check sees every field that can set a recipient: to, cc and bcc, and also the reply fields, because the upstream page for the mail tool says a send needs 'recipients or a reply-all target'. The seeded sends, a reply-all among them, must all be blocked before this goes live.
  • The check blocks a wrong recipient; it does not correct it, because the docs describe rewriting parameters for host-owned tools only.
  • Plain text only: a table arrives as lined-up text, not as a formatted table. A long iMessage already delivers the same text; what this adds is the answer filed in the inbox.
  • Pinning the recipient does not close every way out: the mailed text is often built from research results, and a link in it can carry private text in its address to whoever runs that site once it is clicked. A link is only as trustworthy as the result it came from.
  • No send cap: a runaway loop could fill the asker's own inbox until someone notices or the agent's spend cap stops it.
  • Signing Happy's existing Google account in on the Mac mini for sending is a new use of that account. A send-only grant keeps the token from reading that mailbox, if the installed gog supports it.

Safety Each parent's own agent holds private data and reads outside content, so its mail way out is pinned in code: the house-rules plugin blocks any send not addressed to the calling agent's owner alone, and blocks when the check fails. No mail reader or shared agent gets the tool. Plain text only, so no remote image can report back.

Not verified

  • That the blocking check is called for the mail-out server's send tool and is given every field that can set a recipient: the upstream page names recipients, reply context, a reply-all target and send-as aliases as inputs but does not list the tool's input schema, so whether cc and bcc are separate fields is not known (T5's send-tool turn, then the five-way test).
  • That the check is told which agent is calling, so it can look up that agent's owner; the rule refuses the send when the agent id or the owner lookup is missing (T5).
  • That the installed gog offers a send-only grant (gog auth add --gmail-scope send was read in the upstream command reference) and that the MCP send tool works under it.
  • That gog's MCP write, Gmail-send and tool-filter flags behave as documented on the installed version; the roadmap lists this as not yet confirmed.

Operator platform and guardrails 3

G003

Scheduled jobs: three safety switches and one short jobs script

Needs a buildLow riskOperatorValue 5/5Effort SWave A

Before Happy sends its first scheduled text, three scheduler settings go in: a failed job alerts Tony and not the family, runs missed during a power cut are skipped, and script triggers are off. Every scheduled text is then one job created by one short checked-in script, with its owner's handle read from the family file, a time limit, a tool list, its own daytime hour and its rules in its own message. A job with nothing to say sends nothing.

Example: Jordan's 07:00 mail text fails twice in a row: Tony gets one text from Happy saying so and one more when it recovers, and she is not sent the error. After a power cut the 07:00 text does not turn up at 11:40. To quieten a text, Tony switches that one job off.

Can be built because docs/automation/standing-orders.md:10: OpenClaw's own guide describes giving each recurring program a written scope, trigger, approval gate and escalation rule in AGENTS.md, run on a schedule by automations.

How it works and its limits

How Config first: cron.failureAlert with Tony's handle as its destination, cron.skipMissedJobs: true, cron.triggers.enabled: false. Then test T3: happy-inspect gains one read-only line, automations list --all --json, and one throwaway job is added twice under the same --declaration-key with a changed message; one job afterwards means one add line per job, two means a name-keyed comparison is kept. Then one short checked-in jobs script, applied through the deploy path as the happy user. Every real job the script declares (not T3's throwaway probes) carries --agent, --tz and --timeout-seconds; a job whose text is delivered also carries --to (the owner's handle read from family.json5, never typed in) and --announce, and a test job that must send nothing is declared with --no-deliver. A job that calls the model also carries an explicit --tools list and no --light-context, so the hard rules load on every run; its message holds its rules: begin with the job's label, answer NO_REPLY when there is nothing to say. A text that needs no model is a --command-argv job. Something for both parents is two jobs, one each. No house-rules rule.

Depends on happy-deploy and happy-inspect (exist): the only two scripts Tony's account may run as the happy user; family.json5 (exists): each job's owner handle is read from it; T3 is run first, to show that the deploy path can list the scheduler's jobs. If it cannot, the jobs script is run by hand in the happy session, as M1 did for plugin installs; Tony provides the daytime hour of each scheduled text at execution of that text's own card, where he has not chosen it already (chosen: 07:00 for the mail text, 21:00 Eastern for the evening text)

Limits

  • Failed-job alerts reach Tony as an iMessage from Happy, a deliberate exception to his 'alerts by ntfy' decision: OpenClaw's chat notice carries only a tidied cause, while its webhook would post the raw error text to an outside push service. If iMessage itself is down, the existing Grafana alerts still reach him by ntfy.
  • Alerts start after 2 failures in a row with a 1-hour cooldown. A recurring job is switched off after 10 failures in a row and then disappears from the default job list, which is why the inspect line lists every job, disabled ones included. Without a time limit of its own a model job is bounded only by a 60-minute watchdog, so the script sets one on every job.
  • Switching script triggers off does not stop the no-model jobs that other cards add through this script: OpenClaw's docs list a command job as a separate kind from the script payloads, condition triggers and stream schedules that the switch turns off.
  • After a reboot with FileVault locked nothing fires and nothing alerts; the healthchecks dead-man switch stays the only signal for a Mac that is off. One-off reminders still catch up after an outage even with missed runs skipped.
  • Given up with this form: per-person on and off switches in the family file, automatic clean-up of jobs that no longer match it, and any enforced daily cap or quiet hours. A changed job is applied again by the script if test T3 shows that a job declared again under the same key is updated in place (the wave A runbook read that in the installed code); otherwise it is edited by hand; to quieten Happy, Tony switches a job off or a parent silences the thread on the phone. The comparing generator comes back when the script holds more jobs than can be read at a glance.
  • Reminders Tony sets in chat (F007) are jobs outside the script; the inspect listing shows them beside the scripted ones. The script creates Jordan's jobs too, so her scheduled texts need no command right of her own.

Safety Only restrictive. Script triggers are off before any agent holds the scheduling tool, because they would run with the owning agent's full tool policy. Every job's text goes to its owner alone, whose handle the script reads from the family file; each job has a time limit, and a model job a tool list. Failure alerts go to Tony, not into another person's thread.

Corrected since 9 Oct

  • Diffing against 'automations list --json' is not enough: the list shows enabled jobs only unless --all is passed, so a job disabled by a mute would look missing and be created twice. Use 'automations list --all --json'.

G005

Stopping and checking Happy by text: the built-in commands on one printed sheet

Ready nowLow riskAdults and kidsValue 4/5Effort SWave B

One printed sheet of what already stops and checks Happy, with nothing new built: for Tony, a text that says only 'stop' ends the answer in progress, /new starts a clean chat, and /status, /usage and /tools show health, cost and what Happy can do (documented; not yet tried on iMessage, so the sheet is worded from a five-text test). Jordan is not a command owner, so for her only /new and /reset work; her stop is to tell Tony or, at home, to shut the Mac mini down. The sheet also says what Happy's error line means when the model is down, and what to do about a lost phone.

Example: Tony texts 'stop' when a long answer is heading the wrong way, then '/new'. When a scheduled text starts arriving twice, Jordan tells Tony, and he switches the scheduler off at the Mac.

Combines OCL-06 Built-in chat commands for parents (/stop, /new, /status, /usage, /tools)

Can be built because docs/gateway/security/operator-incident-response.md:15: OpenClaw's incident guide makes stopping the Gateway and freezing who may message it the first containment steps, which this card puts one text away for either parent.

How it works and its limits

How No plugin, no in-house phrase and no rule in the house-rules plugin. First test T8: from his own phone Tony sends 'stop' during a long answer, then /new, /status, /usage and /tools, and notes what comes back; one failed turn is provoked on an eval-only copy of an agent to read the error line a parent would see. The sheet is written from what he saw: the commands that work for Tony (no commands.allowFrom entry is added for Jordan), /new and /reset for Jordan, which words stop one answer, and what stops everything: Tony at the Mac, cron.enabled: false, then openclaw gateway stop. Lost phone, three lines: Find My Lost Mode; Tony removes the handle in family.json5 and redeploys; openclaw devices revoke if that phone ever ran the app. The sheet also says what each scheduled text is and how Tony switches it off, what Happy's error line means, and the photos card's house-rule line (F002).

Depends on T8, run by Tony from his own phone before the sheet is written; The eval-only copy of a parent's agent (exists since M1), for the one provoked failed turn

Limits

  • With an owner list set and no commands.allowFrom, OpenClaw gives the second parent /new and /reset only: her /stop, a bare 'stop', /status, /usage and /tools are dropped without a reply (read from the installed docs and code, not tried from her phone).
  • /stop and the built-in stop words end one answer in one chat and pause no scheduled job, so the sheet says which words stop one answer and which steps stop everything.
  • OpenClaw's stop list has 43 fixed phrases and includes everyday words such as 'exit', 'halt' and 'do not do that': a text that is only one of them ends the answer in progress instead of reaching Happy.
  • Given up with this form: one text from either parent that halts everything while Tony cannot be reached, and a lock-out by text for a lost phone. The phone's own lock screen and Lost Mode cover that gap unless the phone was lost unlocked, and only removing the handle and redeploying ends that handle's approver rights.
  • Shutting the Mac mini down is a stop Jordan cannot undo: after a restart it waits at the disk-unlock screen and Happy stays down until Tony unlocks it.
  • /usage shows local estimates and not the provider's bill, /status and /tools may run long in an iMessage bubble, and /btw and /loop stay off the sheet.

Safety Nothing is built or granted: no plugin, no new command right, no change to who is admitted. Jordan is not authorised for commands, so the commands and directives that authorisation would open (/tts, /compact, /model among them) stay closed to her. Stopping everything and removing a handle stay actions Tony takes at the Mac; /restart and /update stay off.

Corrected since 9 Oct

  • 'Freeze every outbound write' is fail-closed only for tool calls. The phrase matcher and the message_sending check both log and continue when their handler throws or times out, so a broken plugin lets the phrase reach the model and lets scheduled announce texts out. The levels that do not depend on plugin code are the scheduler switch and stopping the Gateway.

Folded in

  • From CRT-02 (Lost or stolen phone: lock one person out): Carry over: an exact lock-out phrase from the other adult suspends one person's handles (no replies, no agent runs or tool calls, no scheduled texts to them) until Tony lifts it at the Mac; the suspension must be enforced in before_agent_run and before_tool_call, which fail closed, because the phrase matcher and message_sending fail open. Also carry the stolen-phone steps: removing the handle from family.json5 and redeploying is the only thing that ends that handle's approver rights, openclaw devices revoke if the phone ran the app, and Find My Lost Mode on the phone side.
  • From CRT-04 (When the model is down: an honest notice, jobs that need no model, and an optional same-vendor fallback): One line on the printed sheet, worded after test T8 has shown a real error text: if Happy answers with an error, the model service is down; try again later.
